 Father Offers 12 Million Yen Reward for Missing Chinese Climber on Mount Fuji
Nov 18, 2026 | News On Japan
 SHIZUOKA -
 The father of a Chinese man who went missing while climbing Mount Fuji has offered a reward of approximately 12 million yen to anyone who finds his son alive, raising concerns that the substantial payment could encourage unauthorized climbers to enter the mountain during its closed season and interfere with official rescue operations.
 The missing man, a Chinese national in his 20s, began climbing Mount Fuji alone from the fifth station of the Yoshida Trail on November 8. He last exchanged messages with a friend shortly before noon that day and has not been heard from since.
 According to Chinese media reports, the man's father has called for volunteers to join the search, offering approximately 12 million yen if his son is found alive and about 2.4 million yen if his body is recovered.
 The announcement has sparked concern on Japanese social media, with users warning that the prospect of a large financial reward could attract inexperienced or poorly equipped individuals to Mount Fuji, potentially putting more lives at risk and obstructing police search and rescue operations.
 The Chinese Embassy in Japan has also urged Chinese nationals to refrain from climbing Mount Fuji and other mountains during their officially closed seasons, emphasizing the dangers associated with winter conditions.
 According to police, search operations on Mount Fuji have been suspended since November 14 because of deteriorating weather conditions. Authorities plan to resume the search once the weather improves.
 Police have reiterated their warning that Mount Fuji is particularly dangerous during the closed climbing season and urged members of the public not to enter the mountain, regardless of the reward being offered.
 The case has drawn attention to the risks of off-season climbing on Japan's highest mountain, where severe weather, freezing temperatures and difficult terrain can make both climbing and rescue operations extremely hazardous.
